human.name: Handedness (JSBP)
human.full_name: Japanese Journal of Biological Psychiatry Handedness Scale
human.description: The JSBP Handedness Inventory is a scale that quantifies handedness by having subjects respond "right," "both," or "left" for 14 different items describing hand preference in various activities.
citations: Okada N, Kasai K, Takahashi T, Suzuki M, Hashimoto R, Kameyama T, Hiramatsu K, Saito O, Niwa S. Rating scale of handedness for biological psychiatry research among Japanese people. Japanese journal of biological psychiatry. 2014; 25(2): 118-9 (in Japanese).

human.name: SES
human.description: A simplified assessment scale that calculates SES based solely on educational background.
citations: Okada N, Kasai K, Takahashi T, Suzuki M, Hashimoto R, Kawakami N. Brief rating scale of socioeconomic status for biological psychiatry research among Japanese people: A scaling based on an educational history. Japanese journal of biological psychiatry. 2014; 25(2): 115-7 (in Japanese)

human.name: JART25
human.full_name: Japanese Adult Reading Test short version
human.description: The Japanese version of the National Adult Reading Test, as a simple method to assess premorbid IQ in patients with mental disorders.
citations: Hirata-Mogi S, Koike S, Toriyama R, Matsuoka K, Kim Y, Kasai K. Reliability of a paper-and-pencil version of the Japanese Adult Reading Test short version. Psychiatry Clin. Neurosci., 70, 362 (2016).

human.name: GAF
human.description: A single-item rating that evaluates the current global functioning of patients.
citations: American Psychiatric Association. Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition, Text Revision (DSM-IV-TR) Washington, DC, USA: American Psychiatric Association; 2000.

human.name: mGAF
human.description: mGAF is a modified version of the original GAF, made to have more detailed criteria and a more structured scoring system.
citations: Hall RC. Global assessment of functioning. A modified scale. Psychosomatics, 36, 267–75 (1995).

Eguchi S, Koike S, Suga M, Takizawa R, Kasai K. Psychological symptom and social functioning subscales of the modified Global Assessment of Functioning scale: reliability and validity of the Japanese version. Psychiatry Clin. Neurosci., 69, 126–7 (2015).

human.name: GAD-7
human.description: The GAD-7 is a screening tool for generalized anxiety disorder and other anxiety disorders, that assesses the frequency of anxiety symptoms across 7 items.
citations: Spitzer RL, Kroenke K, Williams JBW, Löwe B. A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: the GAD-7: The GAD-7. Arch. Intern. Med., 166, 1092–7 (2006).

human.name: BDI-II
human.description: A 21-item self-report inventory measuring the severity of depression.
citations: Beck AT, Steer RA and Brown GK: Manual for the beck depression inventory-II. San Antonio, TX: Psychological Corporation. Psychol Assess, 1996.

Kojima M, Furukawa TA, Takahashi H, Kawai M, Nagaya T and Tokudome S: Cross-cultural validation of the Beck Depression Inventory-II in Japan. Psychiatry Res 110: 291–299, 2002. PMID: 12127479. DOI: 10.1016/s0165-1781(02)00106-3.

human.name: AQ-J-10
human.description: The AQ10 is a shortened version of the AQ50, serving as a 10-item self-report scale to assess traits of Autism Spectrum Disorder。
citations: Kurita H, Koyama T, Osada H. Autism-Spectrum Quotient-Japanese version and its short forms for screening normally intelligent persons with pervasive developmental disorders. Psychiatry Clin. Neurosci., 59, 490–6 (2005).

human.name: BPRS (Oxford)
human.description: A clinician-rated tool that assesses the severity of psychiatric symptoms through the evaluation of 18 items.
citations: Kolakowska T. Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale. Glossaries rating instructions. Oxford University, Oxford, (1976).

human.name: YMRS
human.description: An 11-item clinician-rated scale that assesses the severity of manic symptoms, including elevated mood, increased activity, sleep disturbance, irritability, speech, and thought content.
citations: Young RC, Biggs JT, Ziegler VE, Meyer DA. A rating scale for mania: reliability, validity and sensitivity. Br. J. Psychiatry, 133, 429–35 (1978). https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.133.5.429
Inada T, Inagaki A, Iwamoto K, Nakatani M, Hori H, Higuchi T. Clinical assessment of mania using the Young Mania Rating Scale-J (YMRS-J). Jihou: Revised Edition; 2012.

human.name: HAMD
human.description: A clinician-rated scale that assesses the severity of depressive symptoms, including depressed mood, insomnia, anxiety, and psychomotor symptoms. The 17-item version is used.
citations: Hamilton M. A rating scale for depression. J. Neurol. Neurosurg. Psychiatry, 23, 56–62 (1960). https://doi.org/10.1136/jnnp.23.1.56

Tabuse H, Kalali A, Azuma H, Ozaki N, Iwata N, Naitoh H, Higuchi T, Kanba S, Shioe K, Akechi T, Furukawa TA. The new GRID Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression demonstrates excellent inter-rater reliability for inexperienced and experienced raters before and after training. Psychiatry Res., 153, 61–7 (2007) https://doi.org/10.1016/j.psychres.2006.07.004.

human.name: BE-PSD-J
human.full_name: Brief Evaluation of Psychosis Symptom Domains – Japanese version
human.description: A brief, clinician-rated scale assessing five psychosis-related symptom domains: psychotic symptoms, disorganized thinking, negative symptoms, excitement/mania, and depression/anxiety. Each domain is rated on a 7-point scale from 0 (absent) to 6 (very severe), generally based on symptoms during the past week.
citations: Takeuchi H, et al. Psychometrics of BE-PSD-V2.0 and its correspondence with PANSS and CGI-S. Psychiatry Clin. Neurosci., 80, 417–422 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1111/pcn.70043

# TPDB research metadata — English catalog generated from Google Sheets
This is a study metadata dictionary, not individual participant data or statistical results.
Human data contain measurement categories and variables. Exact cohort availability and sample overlap need confirmation.
Mouse data describe experimental groups and ex vivo MRI acquisition conditions; no mouse-derived regional scalars are provided through TPDB.
Processed mouse MRI images exist outside TPDB. Access conditions, validated cross-species mappings and image-derived measurements must not be inferred.
Missing metadata does not prove underlying data do not exist. Do not force human–mouse research ideas.

## Human measurement categories and variables

Age, gender, and diagnosis. The diagnostic criteria used is also provided
